stories.title: India, Russia set $100 bn trade target for 2030
stories.summary: Indian Ambassador Vinay Kumar said Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin directed their governments to raise bilateral trade to $100 billion and two‑way investment to $50 billion by 2030. The goal was discussed at the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12‑13, and India pledged to supply skilled workers to meet Russian industry needs.
stories.why: The target deepens economic ties and could shift trade and investment patterns between the two large economies.
stories.previousTitle: India and Russia set $100 billion trade goal for 2030
stories.previousSummary: Indian Ambassador Vinay Kumar said India and Russia will work to raise bilateral trade to $100 billion by 2030. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin endorsed the goal during their meeting at the BRICS summit in New Delhi, pledging to boost mutual investments and to train Indian specialists for Russian industries.

stories.title: Three released without charge after fatal arson attack in Ireland
stories.summary: Philip and Kim English and two of their children - nine-year-old Jayden and 12-year-old Callum - died after their home in Birch Avenue, on the outskirts of Waterford was set on fire earlier this month. A man aged in his 20s and a woman in her 30s were previously charged in connection with the attack.

stories.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 results: Consolidated PAT rises 26% YoY to Rs 5,645 crore; NII up 16%

stories.title: German businesses now see India as manufacturing, R&D and innovation hub: Piyush Goyal
stories.summary: German companies are increasingly viewing India as a strategic manufacturing and innovation hub for the future. Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said German companies are increasingly viewing India as a hub for manufacturing, research and development, and innovation, beyond its traditional role as a consumer market.

stories.title: Forced to pick, Grok’s AI model chooses Republicans. OpenAI’s picks Democrats.
stories.summary: A new study found that when forced to choose in this year’s upcoming midterm elections, SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of its answers, while OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol picked the Democrat in 97%. Across nearly 500 races, the two models agreed less than 10% of the time.
stories.why: This matters because it could change AI capabilities, costs, adoption, regulation or competitive positioning.
stories.previousTitle: Study finds Grok favors Republicans, OpenAI model favors Democrats in forced‑choice test
stories.previousSummary: A Convovo study asked SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 and OpenAI’s GPT‑6.1 Sol, via their developer APIs, to name a single candidate for upcoming midterm races without hedging. Grok recommended the Republican candidate in 92% of responses, while GPT‑6.1 Sol chose the Democrat in 97%; the two models agreed on less than 10% of nearly 500 races. Consumer‑facing apps for both services refused to answer the same prompt.
